best_for: People who like the two-pane Total Commander way of working and want a free file manager that behaves the same on Windows, Mac and Linux.

points.title: Free, and modeled on Total Commander
points.text: Double Commander is GPL-2.0 software with no paid tier. It shows two file panels side by side, or one above the other, with tabs, a multi-rename tool, custom columns, a hex and text viewer on F3 and a built-in editor with syntax highlighting on F4.

points.title: Archives open like folders
points.text: You can browse and copy in and out of ZIP, TAR, GZ, BZ2, XZ, LZMA and 7Z archives, and also RPM, CPIO, DEB, RAR and ZIPX, as if they were directories. It loads Total Commander WCX, WDX, WFX and WLX plugins, so many existing add-ons work.

points.title: Remote folders without a separate client
points.text: FTP, FTPS, FTPES, SSH with SCP, and SFTP are built in, and most file operations run in the background while you keep working.

points.title: Windows: MSI packages, machine-wide
points.text: The project says it runs on Windows XP through 11, in 32-bit and 64-bit builds. This listing carries x86 and x64 MSI packages that install for the whole machine; recent ones accept an `APPLICATIONFOLDER` property to set the install path, and 1.0.x releases also include Inno Setup .exe installers. A portable .zip exists on the release page but is not listed here.

points.title: The Mac listing lags behind
points.text: The macOS build uses Cocoa, with Intel and Apple silicon DMGs, and the release page asks for macOS 11 or later. Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Gatekeeper checks, so the Mac version here stays at 1.2.8 while Windows is on 1.2.11.

points.title: Linux and BSD builds are not listed here
points.text: The project ships Linux builds for GTK2, Qt5 and Qt6 as portable archives, AppImages and openSUSE Build Service repositories for Fedora, openSUSE, Debian and Ubuntu. The Qt builds need the libQt5Pas or libQt6Pas bindings. FreeBSD has it in ports, and Haiku support is experimental. None of these are listed here.

points.title: Older builds only for Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 38 versions, back to 0.9.10. macOS keeps only one version, so rolling back on a Mac needs another source.
